channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Armenian PM Pashinyan Pledges Resignation After Peace Deal, Cites NATO Stance
item.description: Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan stated his readiness to resign after signing a peace agreement with Azerbaijan, or if a new constitution is not approved by referendum. He proposed a referendum on the new constitution, suggesting he would step down in either scenario. Pashinyan also mentioned the 'Trump Route' and border delimitation as key steps in the peace process.

item.title: Uzbek Citizen Sentenced to 16 Months in South Korea for Funding Terror Group
item.description: A court in Seoul has sentenced a citizen of Uzbekistan to 16 months in prison for sending funds to a terror group in Syria. The individual was found guilty of violating anti-terrorism laws and ordered to pay a fine. The funds were transferred between January 2024 and January 2025.

item.title: Tanker Truck Overturns and Catches Fire in Shymkent, Driver Dies
item.description: A tanker truck overturned and caught fire in Shymkent following a road accident on the Tashkent highway. Rescuers found the body of a deceased man inside the vehicle's cabin. The fire, which spread to the spilled fuel, was extinguished over an area of 60 square meters.

item.title: Trump, Putin, and Xi to meet at APEC summit in China for first trilateral talks
item.description: US President Donald Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin, and Chinese President Xi Jinping will hold their first trilateral meeting in Shenzhen, China, on November 19. The leaders are expected to discuss international security, nuclear disarmament, and global conflicts on the sidelines of the APEC summit.

item.title: Uzbekistan prioritizes economic potential in Namangan region with new investment projects
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev chaired a meeting focused on boosting reforms, attracting foreign investment, and increasing employment in the Namangan region. The region has significant potential for development through high technology, modern industry, and services, with projected foreign investment reaching $5.4 billion this year.

item.title: Astana to demolish residential building and political party office for LRT construction
item.description: Astana plans to demolish a 1950s residential building and the 'Adilet' party office to make way for the second phase of the light rail transit (LRT) project. The new lines will connect the left bank of the capital with the old railway station, requiring the expropriation of several properties.

item.title: CIS Interparliamentary Assembly Commission Meets in Turkmenistan's Avaza Resort
item.description: Delegations from Azerbaijan, Russia, and Belarus have arrived in Turkmenistan for a meeting of the CIS Interparliamentary Assembly's commission on political issues and international cooperation. The meeting, held in the Avaza resort zone, will discuss Turkmenistan's request for observer status within the CIS IPA.

item.title: Uzbekistan Accelerates New Tashkent Construction and Greening Projects
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev chaired a meeting on accelerating the construction of New Tashkent and the 'Yashil Makon' greening project. New incentives for investors were introduced. The focus is on new approaches, strict discipline, and daily monitoring of investment projects to create favorable conditions and remove obstacles.

item.title: UNICEF Reports 64 Children Killed and 64 Injured in Yemen Amid Escalating Conflict
item.description: UNICEF stated that at least 64 children have been killed and 64 injured in Yemen due to escalating conflict since September 3. The organization warned of further casualties as fighting continues in populated areas and essential services are affected. UNICEF is expanding its emergency response to assist up to 350,000 people.

item.title: OSCE Conference in Ashgabat Focuses on Peace and Parliamentary Diplomacy
item.description: The third Ashgabat Conference, 'The Role of Parliaments in Promoting International Law for Dialogue, Trust, and Security in the OSCE Space,' is underway in Ashgabat. Uzbekistan's delegation, led by the Deputy Speaker of the Legislative Chamber, is participating. The event is organized by the Mejlis of Turkmenistan and the OSCE.

item.title: Uzbekistan Showcases Mining Potential at COP31 Amid Climate Change Concerns
item.description: Uzbekistan is participating in the 31st session of the UN Climate Change Convention (COP31) in Antalya, Turkey, to discuss rational resource use, environmental balance, and industrial adaptation to climate change. The country aims to enhance international cooperation, adopt best practices, and attract investments in its mining sector.

item.title: Three Power Centers Influenced Kazakhstan's National Security Chief's Dismissal
item.description: The recent dismissal of Yermek Sagimbayev as head of Kazakhstan's National Security Committee (KNB) has sparked considerable media and public discussion. While some suggest personal reasons for his departure, sources indicate that Deputy Secretary of the Security Council Aida Balayeva, a group of KNB generals, and figures from the presidential administration influenced the decision.

item.title: Uzbekistan Convicts Four Judges for Unjust Decision in Assault Case
item.description: A district court in Uzbekistan has convicted four former appeals court judges for making an "unjust decision" by reducing a man's sentence in a high-profile assault and fraud case. Prosecutors argued corruption, while the defense claimed the trial undermined judicial independence and reforms.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Afghanistan to Increase Train Traffic on Hairatan-Mazar-i-Sharif Line
item.description: Uzbekistan and Afghanistan have agreed to increase train traffic on the Hairatan-Mazar-i-Sharif railway line. Officials discussed expanding cooperation in the railway sector and noted a significant increase in mutual cargo transportation this year. Both sides will take measures to effectively utilize existing opportunities.

item.title: Turkmenistan Advocates for Climate Diplomacy and Sustainable Development
item.description: Turkmenistan actively participates in international dialogue on sustainable development, emphasizing the expansion of multilateral cooperation to address environmental and climate issues. The country integrates these concerns into its national strategies and collaborates with UN agencies and other organizations to achieve global sustainability goals.

item.title: Pakistan Envoy Discusses Afghanistan, Terrorism Concerns with Swedish Officials
item.description: Pakistan's Special Representative for Afghanistan, Mohammad Sadiq, met with Swedish officials to discuss the situation in Afghanistan, regional security, and concerns over terrorist group activities. Both sides emphasized the importance of joint cooperation to counter emerging terrorist threats and ensure regional stability.

item.title: New Corn Deep Processing Plant Launched in Turkistan Region, Kazakhstan
item.description: A new corn deep processing plant with an annual capacity of 150,000 tons has started operations in Shardara district, Turkistan region. The facility, creating 500 jobs, utilizes modern equipment for nearly 98% waste-free production. It will produce modified starch, gluten, and other derivatives.

item.title: Kazakhstan Focuses on Economic Development for Afghan Stability
item.description: Kazakhstan is contributing to Afghanistan's economic recovery and regional reintegration by prioritizing trade, humanitarian aid, and infrastructure. Astana believes economic development and regional cooperation are key to long-term stability, moving beyond a purely security-focused approach. This strategy aims to create economic opportunities and reconnect Afghanistan with regional networks.

item.title: Zelensky Calls Crimean Bridge Attack an Unprecedented Operation
item.description: President Zelensky described the strike on the Crimean Bridge as an "unprecedented operation" in response to Russian attacks. He stated it was the final stage of a weeks-long operation, involving the destruction of air defense systems and subsequent drone and missile strikes on the bridge's road and rail sections.

item.title: Israeli Army Launches Military Operation in Gaza, Orders Evacuation
item.description: The Israeli army has initiated a military operation in Gaza, ordering residents of three neighborhoods to evacuate. Israeli tanks have entered territory outside of the country's control for the first time since a ceasefire began. Hamas has condemned the operation as a severe violation of the agreement.

item.title: Proposal to Relocate Kyrgyzstan's Capital from Bishkek to Osh Due to Traffic Congestion
item.description: A Kyrgyz parliament member has proposed moving the capital from Bishkek to Osh, citing worsening traffic congestion in the current capital. The proposal suggests learning from Osh's infrastructure development, including new bridges and interchanges. The Minister of Construction noted that Osh's projects began without full documentation.

item.title: Uzbek Professor Sentenced to 10 Years in Prison in Kazakhstan for Espionage
item.description: An Uzbek scholar, Ikboljon Koraboev, detained in Kazakhstan on suspicion of espionage, has been sentenced to 10 years imprisonment. His family learned of the verdict through unofficial sources, as the trial was held in camera. Koraboev, who taught at a university in Astana, denies guilt and intends to appeal.

item.title: New Corn Processing Plant Opens in Turkestan Region, Kazakhstan
item.description: A new corn processing plant, Kazkrakhmal LLP, has begun operations in the Shardara district of Kazakhstan's Turkestan region. The facility is designed to process 150,000 tons of raw corn annually, creating 500 jobs. It will produce modified starch, gluten, and other products, with plans to expand its output to 28 items.

item.title: Woman Dies by Suicide in Faryab Amidst Rising Domestic Violence
item.description: A young woman in Faryab Province, Afghanistan, has died by suicide after reportedly enduring domestic violence. This incident follows similar cases in Paktika and Kandahar. Domestic violence remains a significant social issue, with women and girls disproportionately affected, especially under current restrictions.

item.title: Uzbek President Criticizes "Yashil Makon" Project for High Sapling Mortality
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev criticized the national "Yashil Makon" (Green Space) project, citing that a third of saplings planted in spring have died and reporting irregularities in planting figures. He emphasized that the success metric should be survival and growth, not just the number planted.

item.title: Kazakhstan Opens Central Asia's Largest Feedlot Facility in Turkistan Region
item.description: Kazakhstan has opened Central Asia's largest feedlot complex in the Turkistan Region, capable of fattening up to 50,000 head of cattle annually. The facility, developed by 'Turkistan Agro KZ', covers a full production cycle from feed cultivation to meat processing and sales.

item.title: Uzbekistan Expands Powers of Local Representative Bodies
item.description: Uzbekistan's President has signed a decree to enhance the powers of local representative bodies (Kengashes). The decree mandates regular reporting from local executive authorities, allocates a portion of the local budget directly based on deputy initiatives, and allows citizen observers at sessions.

item.title: Bishkek mayor's office explains lack of heating in "Builders' Town"
item.description: The Bishkek mayor's office stated that residents of "Builders' Town" are experiencing insufficient heating due to unauthorized modifications to the internal heating system. These changes, including pipe narrowing and added bends, disrupt heat circulation. Residents are urged not to alter the system.

item.title: Mossad chief lobbied Washington for joint operation against Iran, Reuters reports
item.description: The head of Israel's Mossad reportedly lobbied Washington for a joint operation against Iran during a visit to the US. The report, citing sources, suggests discussions focused on potential collaborative actions targeting Iran.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Orders Investigation into Russian Investor's Land Dispute
item.description: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov has ordered an investigation into a conflict involving a Russian investor and a local resident in the Issyk-Kul region. The investor claims to have lost $15 million in a project after alleged threats from organized crime groups. The local resident admitted to not investing his own funds and acknowledged ties between construction company leaders and criminal groups.

item.title: Uzbekistan Central Bank Gains Power to Write Off Debts and Transfer Deposits of Troubled Banks
item.description: Uzbekistan's Central Bank has been granted new powers to manage troubled banks through rehabilitation procedures instead of license revocation. Effective November 17, the regulator can now write off debts, transfer assets and liabilities, or create an intermediate bank to resolve issues, aiming to prevent systemic crises and protect depositors.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President Vows Fair, Transparent Presidential Elections
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's President Sadyr Japarov expressed his commitment to ensuring fair and transparent presidential elections. He met with candidates to discuss election preparations and address concerns about administrative resource abuse. Japarov warned state and municipal employees against using their positions to support any candidate, emphasizing equal conditions for all and legal accountability for interference.

item.title: Central Asia's Largest Feedlot Complex Opens in Kazakhstan's Turkestan Region
item.description: Kazakhstan has officially opened its largest feedlot complex in the Turkestan region, capable of fattening up to 50,000 head of cattle annually. The facility, developed with Australian technologies, aims to produce up to 15,000 tons of meat per year and integrates the entire production cycle from feed cultivation to meat processing and sales.

item.title: World Bank: Water Scarcity Threatens Afghanistan's Economic Growth and Employment
item.description: The World Bank reports that water insecurity in Afghanistan is hindering economic growth, employment, energy production, health, and development. Agriculture, which employs 46% of the workforce and uses 95% of water, is particularly vulnerable. Declining river flows could reduce hydropower, and unreliable water access may disrupt economic activities.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President Meets Presidential Candidates, Warns Against Misuse of Administrative Resources
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov met with presidential candidates to hear their concerns and discuss preparations for the upcoming election. He emphasized his personal interest in a clean and fair election, vowing to prevent the misuse of administrative resources and artificial obstacles. Japarov warned state and municipal employees that they serve the people and the state, not him personally.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Meets Investor and Local Figure Over Issyk-Kul Resort Dispute
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov met with Russian investor Dmitry Rebus and local figure Kubat Alymbekov regarding a dispute over a resort on Issyk-Kul Lake. Rebus claimed he invested $15 million but was forced out by organized crime. Alymbekov admitted no personal investment but alleged Rebus reneged on a profit-sharing agreement. The president's brother was mentioned in prior discussions.

item.title: Kazakhstan Proposes Changes to Clinic Appointment Procedures
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Health has proposed changes to how medical services are provided in clinics. The draft project suggests doctors can examine patients, prescribe medication, issue certificates, and provide preventive services during a single appointment if medically indicated. This aims to streamline patient care and improve efficiency within the healthcare system.

item.title: German Institute to Help Navoi Region Machine Builders Access European Markets
item.description: Uzbekistan and Germany's Fraunhofer IPK have signed a memorandum to boost cooperation in machine building. The initiative aims to integrate Navoi region's enterprises into large industrial orders, localize automotive component production, and facilitate access to European markets for local products.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan Consider Restoring 2004 Visa-Free Travel Regime
item.description: Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan have discussed the possibility of restoring the visa-free travel regime from 2004. The parties also discussed launching regular flights on the Tashkent-Ashgabat route and facilitating international cargo transportation. This discussion aims to enhance bilateral ties and ease travel between the two nations.

item.title: Namangan Region Aims for $8 Billion in Foreign Investment and Higher Incomes
item.description: Uzbekistan's President Mirziyoyev reviewed reforms in Namangan region, targeting increased foreign investment to $7-8 billion and average incomes to 9.6 million soms next year. Key projects include modernizing the international airport and developing textile, energy, and pharmaceutical production facilities.
